# Phase Two — Gevurah Architecture and Critique

> The Awtsmoos gives infinite light, yet Gevurah asks which vessels can carry it without break;  
> Awtsmoos.com turns possibility into measured architecture, where every gain must survive the test we make.

## Evidence-Driven Architecture Direction

The prior phase generated many possibilities. Current evidence eliminates several premature choices:

- `ThreeMinuteShowcaseRenderer` is already a small coordinator. Do not bloat it with optimization logic.
- `TiferesMovieDirector` is already a small coordinator. Do not bloat it with feature-generation logic.
- Therefore rendering improvements belong below/around `CinematicFrameRenderer` or in export orchestration, while AI richness belongs below Director in prompt/intent/beat/layer planners.
- The five adapters and canonical movie schema are already verified. Do not destabilize them for unrelated speed work.
- A 2 FPS acceptance render proved media correctness; improvement work must target the gap between that proof sampling and practical higher-FPS production export.

## Proposed Workstreams

### Workstream A — Measured Render Acceleration

Before implementation:

1. Read `CinematicFrameRenderer.js` and its immediate renderer dependencies.
2. Benchmark representative frame times at 0s, 10s, 30s, and 55s for each minute plan.
3. Measure memory and buffer sizes.
4. Determine whether rendering is deterministic when separate renderer instances render the same timestamp.
5. Determine whether multiple renderer instances can execute concurrently in child processes without native Canvas conflicts.

If isolation passes, implement a child-process frame farm as new modules rather than rewriting the cinematic renderer immediately.

Potential files:

- `apps/animator/tools/render/parallel/TiferesRenderWorkerPool.js`
- `apps/animator/tools/render/parallel/MalchusFrameWorker.js`
- `apps/animator/tools/render/parallel/YesodOrderedFrameBuffer.js`
- `apps/animator/tools/render/parallel/ParallelFrameProtocol.js`
- `apps/animator/tools/render/threeMinute/ThreeMinuteParallelExporter.js`
- `apps/animator/tools/render/bench/ThreeMinuteRenderBenchmark.js`

### Workstream B — Richer Deterministic AI Direction

Before implementation:

1. Read `MovieIntentCompiler.js`, `MoviePromptIntent.js`, and `MovieDirectorOutline.js` fully.
2. Record current output for at least five prompts: character story, tutorial, infographic, 3D cinematic product demo, mixed 2D/3D explainer.
3. Score current semantic kinds, camera variety, scene purposes, text/chart/character/particle/world coverage.

Then split new planning responsibilities into small modules rather than growing one compiler:

- prompt vocabulary/feature extraction;
- scene-purpose planner;
- semantic layer composer;
- camera grammar;
- infographic/tutorial grammar;
- deterministic style/seed planner;
- richness/coverage report.

### Workstream C — Studio Capability and Quality UX

Only after A/B contracts are stable:

- show canonical scene richness and target fidelity;
- show quick/balanced/quality render profile semantics;
- keep quality controls separate from movie content;
- expose native/fallback/deferred status per target studio;
- mobile-first compact disclosure rather than giant desktop panels.

## 24 Critiques / Improvements to Phase One

1. Do not parallelize before proving renderer-instance isolation.
2. Do not use worker threads until native Canvas worker safety is measured.
3. Prefer child processes first because process isolation contains native addon state.
4. Avoid sending full plans with every frame request; initialize worker once, then send frame indices/times.
5. Keep a bounded number of in-flight frames to prevent RAM explosions.
6. Preserve ordered ffmpeg input even when workers finish out of order.
7. Hash sequential vs parallel frames at identical timestamps to prove equivalence.
8. Benchmark warm renderer performance separately from constructor/startup cost.
9. Measure single-process baseline after any concurrent system load settles.
10. Never claim speedup from wall time if machine load differs wildly; report frame throughput and test conditions.
11. Add cancellation so long exports can stop workers cleanly.
12. Add worker retry only for deterministic recoverable failures; do not infinite-loop corrupt frames.
13. Keep the existing sequential exporter as a fallback path.
14. Avoid modifying `ThreeMinuteShowcaseRenderer` unless profiling identifies a local hot operation.
15. Pre-index `featureBeats` only if benchmark shows lookup matters; array search over a tiny set may be irrelevant.
16. AI richness must be validated from output semantics, not metadata claims.
17. Prompt extraction must preserve explicit user constraints over inferred defaults.
18. Genre inference must not force one style when the prompt is ambiguous.
19. Scene-purpose planning must work for arbitrary durations, not only the 180-second fixture.
20. Camera grammar must avoid nauseating constant motion; purpose drives movement.
21. Tutorial/infographic layers should remain renderer-neutral and adapter-friendly.
22. Style seeds should make deterministic fallback repeatable across runs.
23. Studio UI should reveal fidelity without implying all 3D layers render natively everywhere.
24. Quality presets must never silently alter canonical project duration/content.

## Failure Map

- Parallel worker crashes -> preserve sequential fallback and bounded retry.
- Native Canvas conflict -> fall back to child-process isolation or scene-chunk model.
- IPC overhead erases speedup -> measure; switch to larger chunks or encoded segment strategy.
- Memory spikes -> cap queue depth and workers.
- AI output validates but is boring -> semantic coverage score and prompt-specific assertions.
- Rich AI output becomes visually incoherent -> style bible + scene-purpose continuity.
- Mobile UX becomes denser -> progressive disclosure and compact summaries.
- Concurrent agents overwrite work -> fresh status/hash check immediately before every rewrite.

## Phase-Two File Touch Policy

No existing hot-path file will be rewritten until it has been freshly read after this plan and benchmarked. Prefer new modules around stable cores. Any existing-file rewrite must be a full-file rewrite and preceded by collision/hash evidence.
